subject: how to set the file location when open_progress  is true

messages.author: 0d4085b4474fa32a
messages.subject: how to set the file location when open_progress  is true
parts:
Hi!
I'm running rstan through a server with multiple cores, and I couldn't find a way to check the progress. If I set a diagnostic_file, it will be stored in the folder where  the script is located, but I couldn't find where the file with the progress is. Is there a way to set it up?

Thanks!

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: how to set the file location when open_progress  is true
parts:
On Sunday, August 23, 2015 at 9:50:32 AM UTC-4, Bruno Nicenboim wrote:
I'm running rstan through a server with multiple cores, and I couldn't find a way to check the progress. If I set a diagnostic_file, it will be stored in the folder where  the script is located, but I couldn't find where the file with the progress is. Is there a way to set it up?

The diagnostic_file is not intended to be used for progress checking. If it is a Linux server, you could just use screen or whatever and periodically log back in to see what iteration it has completed. I fear you are talking about a Windows server, in which case I guess you could just leave Internet Explorer open and refresh it periodically. It is not possible to specify a file to write the progress to but it is a randomly named file in tempdir() so you could call tempdir() before calling Stan to see what that directory is and open the resulting progress file some other way.

Ben
